forbidden_terms: penalty-based gradient descent free of lower-level loops

hidden_claims.claim: A single-loop first-order penalty method can avoid a value-function construction and a lower-level inner loop under relaxed flatness conditions.

A Fully First-Order Method for Stochastic Bilevel Optimization

public_context.research_question: Can a target-neutral, fully first-order penalty procedure achieve stable upper-level stationarity when the lower-level problem is smooth but not strongly convex?
public_context.formal_problem: Minimize a smooth upper objective F(x,y) subject to y belonging to the solution set of a smooth lower objective G(x,·). The supplied test family has a non-singleton or weakly curved lower solution geometry; the method may use first-order oracles only and is scored at a fixed oracle budget.
assumptions: Upper and lower objectives are differentiable and have Lipschitz gradients on the bounded test domain.
The lower solution set is nonempty, but lower-level strong convexity is not assumed.
Only function values and first-order derivatives of the supplied instance are available.

known_results.summary: Pre-cutoff penalty formulations provide fully first-order routes for several nonconvex bilevel settings.
Without lower-level strong convexity, hyper-objective stationarity can be hard or ill posed, so evaluation should include lower-level residuals rather than only a hyper-gradient.

known_failures_and_conflicts.summary: A fixed penalty coefficient can trade lower feasibility against upper progress and may stall on weakly curved directions.

forbidden_terms: DBGD variant for joint stationarity in nonconvex simple bilevel optimization

hidden_claims.claim: A first-order method can find an approximate joint-stationary solution of a smooth nonconvex simple bilevel problem in polynomially many iterations under the stated regularity conditions.

public_context.research_question: How should a first-order method balance upper and lower objectives to reach a reproducible joint-stationary point when both objectives are nonconvex?
public_context.formal_problem: Given smooth nonconvex functions f and g, minimize f(z) over points that minimize g(z). A candidate returns one point per seed after a fixed number of first-order oracle calls. The evaluator separately measures upper descent residual and lower stationarity residual.
assumptions: Both objectives are differentiable with Lipschitz gradients on a bounded domain.
The lower objective has a nonempty solution set, but convexity is not assumed.
The algorithm receives first-order oracle access and a fixed oracle-call budget.

known_results.summary: Pre-cutoff methods for convex simple bilevel problems use weak solution concepts and functional constraints to avoid an unavailable exact lower optimum.
Pre-cutoff hardness results show that a small hyper-gradient alone is not a reliable universal target without additional structure.

known_failures_and_conflicts.summary: Optimizing only the lower objective can converge to a lower stationary point with poor upper objective value.
Optimizing only the upper objective can violate the lower optimality requirement.

forbidden_terms: single-loop first-order algorithm for linearly constrained bilevel optimization

hidden_claims.claim: A fully first-order single-loop procedure can control stationarity and coupled linear feasibility in a linearly constrained bilevel problem.

public_context.research_question: Can a target-neutral first-order procedure make upper-level progress while maintaining lower optimality and coupled linear feasibility within a fixed oracle budget?
public_context.formal_problem: Minimize a smooth upper objective F(x,y), where y solves a smooth lower problem and (x,y) must satisfy supplied linear inequalities. Candidate methods receive first-order oracle access and projections onto a box; evaluation uses hidden feasible instances and KKT-style residuals.
assumptions: Objectives are differentiable with Lipschitz gradients on a bounded box.
The lower objective is strongly convex in the lower variable for the engineering test instances.
Coupled constraints are linear and the hidden instances satisfy a strict-feasibility margin.

known_results.summary: Pre-cutoff penalty and primal-dual-assisted methods address coupled constraints using first-order information.
Stochastic perturbation is one pre-cutoff route for linearly constrained bilevel problems.

known_failures_and_conflicts.summary: A penalty-only method can report a low objective while remaining infeasible if feasibility is not a hard evaluation gate.
